verdicts.title: Security modifiers onlyOwner/onlyManager are no-ops

a.reden: Both describe the ineffective onlyOwner/onlyManager modifiers in Security.sol that lack require/revert, making privileged functions public.

b.reden: Both findings describe the same bug where onlyOwner/onlyManager modifiers lack require/revert making them no-ops.

verdicts.title: FeeSplitter.setCurves callable by anyone to hijack fee accounting

a.reden: Both describe the unrestricted setCurves function in FeeSplitter allowing anyone to change the Curves reference

b.reden: Both describe the same root cause: the unprotected setCurves function allowing anyone to change the Curves reference.

verdicts.title: Missing access control on Security modifiers allows anyone to bypass onlyOwner/onlyManager

a.reden: Both describe the ineffective onlyOwner/onlyManager modifiers in Security.sol that lack require/revert, resulting in unrestricted access.

b.reden: Both describe the same missing access control due to modifiers without require/revert in Security.sol.

verdicts.title: Security modifiers missing revert — access control completely bypassed

a.reden: Both describe the same missing revert in the onlyOwner modifier in Security.sol, leading to ineffective access control.

b.reden: Both findings describe the same access control bypass in Security.sol modifiers onlyOwner and onlyManager due to missing revert.

a.reden: The candidate describes a different function (CurvesERC20Factory.deploy) and issue not covered by any known finding.

b.reden: The candidate describes a permissionless factory deployment issue, which is unrelated to the known findings about fee distribution, honeypot, FeeSplitter access control, or modifier logic.

verdicts.title: FeeSplitter.onBalanceChange resets user offset, wiping accrued holder fees

a.reden: Both describe the same flaw in FeeSplitter.onBalanceChange where the user fee accumulator is not properly updated, causing loss of accrued holder fees.

b.reden: Both describe the same root cause: onBalanceChange resets user offset without updating accrued fees, leading to loss of holder fees.

verdicts.title: buyCurvesTokenWhitelisted allows buying before presale start

b.reden: No known finding addresses presale start time enforcement in buyCurvesTokenWhitelisted.

verdicts.title: _transferFees reverts entire trade if any fee recipient rejects ETH

a.reden: Both describe the same _transferFees function where failing external calls (e.g., referralFeeDestination) cause the whole trade to revert, enabling a honey‑pot style denial of service.

b.reden: Both findings describe the same root cause where _transferFees reverts on failed ETH transfer to user-controlled addresses like referralFeeDestination, allowing a malicious subject to block sells.

b.reden: Both findings identify that FeeSplitter does not update user fee credits during token transfers, deposits, or withdrawals.
